extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom leaders, journalism grantees, and philanthropy/funder partners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy from a foundation (Democracy Fund) on supporting, funding, and protecting journalism that advances pro-democracy movements and racial equity, including an editorial firewall policy to preserve grantee editorial independence. The page describes funding priorities, program goals, and specific rules for funder–grantee communications and disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-engaged journalism that drives civic engagement and anti-racist outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: "When reporters are deeply involved with the communities they report for and about, there is a greater understanding of what information drives people to become civically engaged and anti-racist."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism should be produced with deep involvement in the communities covered so reporting better understands and delivers the information that motivates civic engagement and supports anti-racist outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformative journalism advancing fairness, inclusion, and justice
rubrics_metrics.description: "To produce journalism that advocates for fairness, inclusion, and justice, we must first transform the way journalism operates. We champion the power of journalists and publishers to support communities of color to create media that strengthens the movement for an inclusive, multiracial democracy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize changes to media systems, newsroom composition, and editorial practices so journalism actively advances equity and justice rather than perpetuating bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding priority: Newsrooms that advance pro-democracy movements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journalism and Power Building Initiative invests in "Newsrooms that advance pro-democracy movements."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for funding news organizations whose reporting and programming explicitly support democratic participation, accountability, and movement-building goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding priority: Expanding campaigns and organized efforts to change journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journalism and Power Building Initiative invests in "Expanding campaigns and organized efforts to change journalism."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support is directed to collective, organized efforts (campaigns, coalitions, advocacy) that seek to reform journalism practices, ownership, or systems at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding priority: Providing leaders with resources to transform journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journalism and Power Building Initiative invests in "Providing individual leaders with the resources they need to transform journalism."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in leadership development, capacity-building, and resourcing for individual journalists and newsroom leaders who can drive institutional change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial firewall: grantee contact protocol (use communications team)
rubrics_metrics.description: "In the instance of a grantee approaching a member of our staff for comment, we require them to go through our communications team — not a program officer."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When grantees contact funder staff for comment, the communications team should handle requests rather than program officers to maintain separation between funding/program decisions and editorial interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial firewall: alert reporters of funding relationship and request disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: "We alert the reporter of the funding relationship. We also request that if they quote a member of our team they disclose our funding of their organization in any story produced."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funder should proactively inform reporters about the funding relationship and ask that articles disclose the funder's support when quoting funder staff, ensuring transparency in coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial firewall: communications staff must not pitch grantee newsrooms
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Democracy Fund communications staff does not send pitches to the nonprofit newsrooms we support."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications teams should avoid promotional outreach (pitches) to organizations they fund to prevent perceived or real influence over editorial agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial firewall: grant agreements include non-interference language
rubrics_metrics.description: "We include language in our grant agreements that we won’t discuss editorial content with journalism grantees or otherwise seek to influence their coverage."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant contracts should explicitly state the funder will not engage in discussions about editorial content or attempt to influence reporting, preserving editorial independence contractually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial firewall: permissible engagement with newsroom leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: "However, we may alert newsroom leadership of Democracy Fund developments and news in the course of regular engagement with grantees."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While avoiding editorial interference, funders may share organizational updates with newsroom leadership as part of normal relationship management; such communications should not cross into editorial direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Square goal: ensure every community has access to accurate information
rubrics_metrics.description: "Public Square strategies seek to ensure every community in the United States has access to accurate information that encourages healthy, informed, and engaged lives."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should be evaluated on their ability to expand equitable access to factual information across diverse communities to support civic health and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil and Human Rights Online principle: hold platforms accountable for hate speech and false information
rubrics_metrics.description: "For many people, being online means being exposed to a toxic environment where hate speech and false information is unavoidable. ... social media companies must be held accountable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts should include strategies to reduce online harms and push for platform accountability as part of information ecosystem work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable Civic Infrastructure principle: promote community-driven media policy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Everything we read, watch, and hear is shaped by policy decisions. ... we need new media policy that’s driven by our communities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for media and technology policy reforms that are shaped by community needs and that counteract policies favoring large media and tech incumbents.
